title: Unit 2 Practice Questions

options: Production of large number of offspring
Independence from external aquatic medium for gamete fusion
questions.correctAnswer: Independence from external aquatic medium for gamete fusion

options: Viviparous animals have higher offspring survival rate
External fertilization is common in water

questions.question: The mode in which embryo develops outside the mother is:

options: Embryo gets nutrition from yolk only
Embryo gets continuous nutrition from mother
questions.correctAnswer: Embryo gets continuous nutrition from mother

questions.question: Which of the following shows internal fertilization, retention of eggs, and live birth with yolk nutrition?
Which of the following combinations correctly matches an animal characteristic with its functional advantage in a changing environment?
options: Heterotrophic nutrition – ability to colonise nutrient-poor soils
Radial symmetry – rapid response to unilateral stimuli
Bilateral symmetry – efficient forward locomotion and cephalization
Multicellularity – independent survival of individual cells after injury
questions.correctAnswer: Bilateral symmetry – efficient forward locomotion and cephalization

questions.question: Which statement about homeothermic animals is incorrect?
options: They maintain a nearly constant core temperature through high basal metabolic rate.
Their enzyme systems function optimally over a wide range of external temperatures.
They can remain fully active at ambient temperatures far below their core temperature.
questions.correctAnswer: Their enzyme systems function optimally over a wide range of external temperatures.

questions.question: An animal has the following features: chitinous exoskeleton, jointed appendages, three pairs of legs, and one pair of antennae. It belongs to:
Homeothermic animals can occupy a wider range of habitats than poikilothermic animals of similar size mainly because:
options: They rely only on behavioural thermoregulation.
Their enzyme systems remain efficient across a wide range of external temperatures.
questions.correctAnswer: Their enzyme systems remain efficient across a wide range of external temperatures.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most significant evolutionary advantage of internal fertilization over external fertilization for terrestrial insects?
options: It allows the female to produce millions of eggs at once.
It allows the male to choose the strongest female.
It prevents the gametes (sperm and egg) from drying out in the air.
It eliminates the need for a pupal stage.
questions.correctAnswer: It prevents the gametes (sperm and egg) from drying out in the air.

questions.question: During which stage of complete metamorphosis is Juvenile Hormone present at its lowest level?
Why are insects particularly vulnerable immediately after moulting?
options: They lose all their legs temporarily
The new cuticle is soft and has not yet hardened
questions.correctAnswer: The new cuticle is soft and has not yet hardened

questions.question: Which statement about frog eggs is correct?
options: They have a hard shell like bird eggs
They are amniotic and can be laid on dry land
They undergo internal fertilisation in most species
They are covered by a jelly-like substance and must usually be laid in water
questions.correctAnswer: They are covered by a jelly-like substance and must usually be laid in water

questions.question: Most amphibians are:
External fertilisation is characteristic of:
The main advantage of complete metamorphosis in insects is that:
options: It allows the insect to live permanently in water
It eliminates the need for moulting
The larva and adult usually do not compete for the same resources
questions.correctAnswer: The larva and adult usually do not compete for the same resources

questions.question: Which hormone keeps an insect larva from turning into a pupa or adult?
A grasshopper belongs to which type of development?
Which combination is correct for birds?

options: Protect the eggs from drying and some predators
questions.correctAnswer: Protect the eggs from drying and some predators

questions.question: The stage in complete metamorphosis during which the body is almost completely rebuilt is the:
The main difference between oviparous and viviparous animals is:
options: Whether the embryo develops outside or inside the mother's body with maternal nourishment
The presence or absence of metamorphosis
Whether they live on land or in water
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the embryo develops outside or inside the mother's body with maternal nourishment

questions.question: An animal that lays eggs which hatch outside the mother's body is described as:
Which of the following is a correct comparison?
options: Insect pupa and frog tadpole both are free-swimming
Both insects and frogs produce amniotic eggs
Insect larva and frog tadpole both function mainly in feeding and growth
Adult insects and adult frogs both breathe only with gills
questions.correctAnswer: Insect larva and frog tadpole both function mainly in feeding and growth

questions.question: The process of shedding the old exoskeleton in insects is called:
Crocodiles have internal fertilization and lay hard leathery eggs. Which of the following best explains the adaptive advantage of this combination over the reproductive strategy of frogs?
options: It provides better protection of the embryo from desiccation and mechanical damage
It enables fertilization to occur on land
It eliminates the need for parental care
It allows a greater number of offspring to be produced
questions.correctAnswer: It provides better protection of the embryo from desiccation and mechanical damage

questions.question: The number of eggs laid by a crocodile ranges from 10 to 100. The most likely evolutionary reason for this wide range is:
options: High and unpredictable mortality of eggs and hatchlings
Variation in female body size only
Seasonal changes in food availability for the female
questions.correctAnswer: High and unpredictable mortality of eggs and hatchlings

questions.question: In birds, the majority of species are monogamous. The primary selective advantage of monogamy in most birds is:
options: Greater efficiency in territorial defence by a single pair
Reduction in the risk of sexually transmitted diseases
Shared parental investment that improves chick survival
questions.correctAnswer: Shared parental investment that improves chick survival

questions.question: Male birds lack external genitalia. The most important functional consequence of this is:
options: Sperm transfer must occur via the cloaca
Mating can only occur during flight
questions.correctAnswer: Sperm transfer must occur via the cloaca

questions.question: In the avian oviduct, nearly all the albumen is secreted in the magnum. If the magnum were surgically shortened, the most immediate effect on the egg would be:
options: Failure of the hard shell to form
A thinner or incomplete egg white layer
Inability of the egg to be laid
questions.correctAnswer: A thinner or incomplete egg white layer

questions.question: The hard shell of a bird's egg is deposited in the uterus (shell gland). The relatively long time the egg spends in this region is necessary because:
options: Complete deposition of calcium carbonate requires extended time
Fertilization occurs only in the uterus
questions.correctAnswer: Complete deposition of calcium carbonate requires extended time

questions.question: A brood patch develops in many incubating birds. Its primary physiological function is to:
options: Produce hormones that maintain incubation behaviour
Store extra fat for the parent
Increase blood flow and heat transfer to the eggs
Protect the parent's skin from the rough eggshell
questions.correctAnswer: Increase blood flow and heat transfer to the eggs

questions.question: The egg tooth of a hatching chick is a temporary structure. Its presence indicates that:
options: The parents must help open the egg
Mechanical force is required to break the rigid eggshell
The chick feeds on the eggshell after hatching
questions.correctAnswer: Mechanical force is required to break the rigid eggshell

questions.question: In rats, the testes are located in the scrotum. The most important physiological reason for this position is:
options: Maintenance of a temperature slightly lower than core body temperature for normal spermatogenesis
Storage of large quantities of sperm
Easier transfer of sperm during mating
questions.correctAnswer: Maintenance of a temperature slightly lower than core body temperature for normal spermatogenesis

questions.question: Female rats possess two uterine horns. This anatomical feature is directly related to:
options: The ability to produce large litters
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to produce large litters

questions.question: After fertilization in rats, the zygote forms a blastocyst that implants in the uterine horn. Implantation is essential because it:
options: Allows the embryo to receive nutrients and oxygen via the placenta
Triggers the formation of the egg tooth
Enables the embryo to breathe air
questions.correctAnswer: Allows the embryo to receive nutrients and oxygen via the placenta

questions.question: The placenta of the rat performs which dual function?
options: Transport of oxygen to the embryo and removal of metabolic wastes
Production of milk and removal of carbon dioxide
Digestion of yolk and secretion of albumen
Formation of the amniotic sac and umbilical cord
questions.correctAnswer: Transport of oxygen to the embryo and removal of metabolic wastes

questions.question: Newborn rats are hairless, deaf and have sealed eyelids. These characteristics indicate that rats are:
In rats, parental care is provided exclusively by the female. The most important consequence of this pattern is:
options: The nest is always built by the male
Males can mate with multiple females in a short time
questions.correctAnswer: Males can mate with multiple females in a short time

questions.question: Which combination of structures is present in the male rat but absent in the male bird?
Which of the following best explains why male rats do not participate in parental care while many male birds do?
options: The reproductive strategy and certainty of paternity differ between the two groups
Both B and C are correct
Rat pups are born at a more advanced stage than bird chicks
Male rats lack mammary glands and therefore cannot feed the young
questions.correctAnswer: The reproductive strategy and certainty of paternity differ between the two groups

questions.question: Which of the following combinations correctly lists only fundamental characteristics shared by all animals?
options: Eukaryotic, multicellular, autotrophic, presence of cell wall
Eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic, motile at some stage
questions.correctAnswer: Eukaryotic, multicellular, heterotrophic, motile at some stage

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes vertebrates from invertebrates?
options: Vertebrates possess a vertebral column; invertebrates lack a backbone
Invertebrates have a closed circulatory system; vertebrates have an open one
Only invertebrates show bilateral body symmetry
All vertebrates are cold-blooded while all invertebrates are warm-blooded
questions.correctAnswer: Vertebrates possess a vertebral column; invertebrates lack a backbone

questions.question: All of the following are true of invertebrates EXCEPT:
options: They represent the most diverse group of animals
Many are soft-bodied or possess a chitinous exoskeleton
They possess a well-defined internal skeleton of cartilage and bone
questions.correctAnswer: They possess a well-defined internal skeleton of cartilage and bone

questions.question: The axial skeleton of a vertebrate includes all of the following EXCEPT:

External fertilization is most accurately characterized by:
options: Release of eggs into an aqueous environment where sperm fertilize them
Fusion of gametes inside the female's reproductive tract
Development of eggs without any sperm involvement
Internal development of the embryo after fertilization
questions.correctAnswer: Release of eggs into an aqueous environment where sperm fertilize them

questions.question: The immediate product of fertilization is a:
Organogenesis refers to:
options: The rapid cell divisions immediately after fertilization
The formation of organs from the germ layers during embryonic development
questions.correctAnswer: The formation of organs from the germ layers during embryonic development

questions.question: Which animal is both an invertebrate and typically possesses a chitinous exoskeleton?
A poikilothermic vertebrate would most likely be:
options: Only animals that live exclusively on land

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: The germ layers formed during gastrulation give rise to different tissues and organ systems
Asexual reproduction is more common among vertebrates than among invertebrates
Vertebrates have a centralized nervous system with a brain and sensory organs
Invertebrates are the most diverse group of animals and are found nearly everywhere
questions.correctAnswer: Asexual reproduction is more common among vertebrates than among invertebrates

questions.question: The lining of the digestive tract (gut) and the respiratory tract develops from the:
Which of the following structures is derived from the mesoderm?
options: Heart, blood vessels and skeletal muscles
questions.correctAnswer: Heart, blood vessels and skeletal muscles

questions.question: The liver and pancreas are formed from which germ layer?
Which combination is correctly matched?
options: Endoderm → Lining of gut, lungs, liver and pancreas
questions.correctAnswer: Endoderm → Lining of gut, lungs, liver and pancreas
